about.title: Truckee Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Truckee's mountain terrain and heavy snow season create conditions property owners are expected to manage — cleared entryways, salted parking lots, dry lobby floors. When a store, rental cabin, ski resort building, or restaurant along Donner Pass Road or near the I-80 corridor fails to address a known hazard, the people who get hurt are often left covering medical bills alone. California premises liability law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the ice patch, spill, or broken step and did nothing about it. Because Truckee sees seasonal tourist traffic alongside year-round residents, businesses face regular foot traffic that raises the standard of upkeep expected of them. If you slipped, tripped, or fell on someone else's property here, documenting the scene quickly matters — snow melts, spills get mopped up, and surveillance footage can be overwritten within days. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options.

items.title: We Understand the Notice Requirement
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. The attorney we connect you with can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: We Emphasize Preserving Evidence Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage from a Truckee hotel, grocery store, or ski lodge is often deleted within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make a real difference in how a claim is evaluated.

items.title: We Account for Comparative Fault Rules
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced by your own percentage of fault but isn't automatically barred. An independent attorney can help present the facts fairly rather than let an insurer overstate your share of blame.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Truckee?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity — a public trail, county building, or transit stop — that deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. Because these timelines are strict, it's worth having an attorney review the facts sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell because of ice or snow that seemed unavoidable in a mountain town like Truckee?
items.answer: Snow and ice are common here, but property owners still have a duty to clear walkways, entrances, and parking areas within a reasonable time or warn people of icy conditions. Whether a hazard was reasonably foreseeable and addressed is exactly the kind of question an attorney can evaluate using maintenance records and weather timing. The fact that snow is common in Truckee doesn't automatically excuse an owner from responsibility.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service — we are not a law firm and we don't charge you anything to be matched with an independent attorney. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
